overall: Atlanta is starting Juneteenth under a solid overcast (OVC, ceiling ~700 ft) with the temperature sitting at 73.4°F as of 04:19 ET — notably, this is already the running daily max, meaning temps have been flat or slightly dipping overnight after a brief early-morning rise. Active Flash Flood Warnings (expiring ~5:45 AM) and Flood Watch coverage across central/west-central Georgia signal a very moist, saturated boundary layer with dewpoints near 70°F, which will limit the diurnal temperature range. The west wind at ~10-13 mph should help with daytime mixing once the overcast breaks.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models are in unusually tight agreement: ECMWF 84.4°F, HRRR 84.6°F, and NBM 84.1°F all cluster within a half-degree around 84-85°F, while the NWS text forecast calls for a slightly warmer 86°F. The intraday model's probability mode sits in the 86-87°F bucket (27.6%), reflecting some upside skew, but the tight NWP consensus and the high early-morning cloud cover (plus wet antecedent soils from recent flooding) suggest the NWP 84-85°F target may be slightly more reliable than the text forecast's 86°F.
max_temp_prediction: The current running max of 73.4°F at 4 AM requires roughly 11-12°F of daytime warming to reach the NWP consensus of ~84-85°F — very achievable for mid-June Atlanta once cloud cover breaks and solar heating ramps up. However, the saturated soils (post-flood), moist air mass (dewpoint ~70°F), and potential for afternoon convection (20% PoP 2-4 PM per NWS) all act as modest caps on sensible heating, slightly favoring the lower end of the NWP range. Confidence is moderate-to-good given the strong NWP model agreement; best estimate is approximately 85.5°F, with the 84-87°F range covering most of the probability mass.
